source_text: Quae si quis consideret et examinet, tractatu longo atque argumentis opus non est. Probatio est ad fidem facilis compendio veritatis. Loquitur Dominus ad Petrum: Ego tibi dico, inquit, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, et portae inferorum non vincent eam. Et tibi dabo claves regni coelorum: et quae ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in coelis; et quaecumque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in coelis. Et iterum eidem post resurrectionem suam dicit: Pasce oves meas. Super illum unum aedificat Ecclesiam suam, et illi pascendas mandat oves suas. Et quamvis Apostolis omnibus post resurrectionem suam parem potestatem tribuat et dicat, Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos: accipite Spiritum sanctum; si cujus remiseritis peccata, remittentur illi, si cujus tenueritis, tenebuntur, tamen, ut unitatem manifestaret, unam cathedram constituit, unitatis ejusdem originem ab uno incipientem sua auctoritate disposuit. Hoc erant utique et caeteri Apostoli quod fuit Petrus, pari consortio praediti et honoris et potestatis, sed exordium ab unitate proficiscitur, et primatus Petro datur, ut una Christi Ecclesia et cathedra una monstretur. Et pastores sunt omnes, et grex unus ostenditur, qui ab Apostolis omnibus unanimi consensione pascatur, ut Ecclesia Christi una monstretur. Quam unam Ecclesiam etiam in Cantico canticorum Spiritus sanctus ex persona Domini designat et dicit: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genitrici suae. Hanc Ecclesiae unitiatem qui non tenet, tenere se fidem credit? Qui Ecclesiae renititur et resistit, qui cathedram Petri, super quem fundata est Ecclesia, deserit, in Ecclesia se esse confidit? quando et beatus apostolus Paulus hoc idem doceat et sacramentum unitatis ostendat dicens: Unum corpus et unus spiritus, una spes vocationis vestrae, unus Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma, unus Deus.
pass_a_gloss: If someone considers and examines these things, a long treatment and arguments are not needed. The proof is easy for faith by a summary of truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: I say to you, he says, that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of the underworld will not conquer it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatever you bind on earth, will be bound also in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth, will be loosed also in heaven. And again he says to him after his resurrection: Feed my sheep. He builds his Church on this one, and he entrusts his sheep to be fed to him. And although he gives equal power to all the Apostles after his resurrection and says, As the Father sent me, and I send you: receive the Holy Spirit; if you remit the sins of anyone, they will be remitted to them, if you retain those of anyone, they will be retained, nevertheless, in order to show unity, he establishes one chair, and he arranges the origin of this unity to begin from one by his authority. The other Apostles were certainly the same as Peter, endowed with equal partnership and honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and the primacy is given to Peter, so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that one Church of Christ may be shown. The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord, and says: My dove is one, my perfect one, one to her mother, chosen by her parent. Who does not hold this unity of the Church, believes that he holds the faith? Who resists and opposes the Church, and deserts the chair of Peter, on which the Church is founded, is confident that he is in the Church? When even the blessed Apostle Paul teaches this same thing and shows the sacrament of unity, saying: One body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God.

bible_refs.note: keys of the kingdom of heaven

pass_b_english: A brief look at these matters makes long arguments unnecessary; the truth sums itself up in a way faith grasps at once.

The Lord says to Peter, "You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of the underworld will not conquer it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven" (Matt 16:18–19).
After the resurrection he tells him again, "Feed my sheep" (John 21:17), and he builds his Church on this one man, entrusting his flock to his care.

True, the risen Lord gives all the apostles equal authority — "As the Father sent me, so I send you. Receive the Holy Spirit; if you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven; if you retain them, they are retained" — yet to make unity visible he establishes a single chair, decreeing by his own authority that this unity must spring from one source.
The other apostles shared Peter's rank, honor, and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and the primacy is given to Peter so that Christ's Church and its chair may be seen as one.
All are shepherds, yet there is only one flock, fed by the apostles with one consent, so that the oneness of Christ's Church may be shown.
The Holy Spirit points to this same unity in the Song of Songs, speaking in the Lord's person: "My dove is one, my perfect one, one to her mother, chosen by her parent."

Anyone who fails to hold this unity of the Church cannot claim to hold the faith. Anyone who resists the Church and abandons the chair of Peter, on which the Church is founded, cannot be confident he belongs to the Church.
Even the blessed apostle Paul teaches the same truth and displays the sacrament of unity: "One body and one Spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God" (Eph 4:4–6).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning and adds necessary scripture citations (Matthew 16:18–19, John 21:17, Ephesians 4:4–6) which correspond correctly to the quoted/alluded text. The title 'Unity of the Church' correctly names the thought of the chapter.
